Peccadillo

pek-uh-DIL-oh · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Peccadillo is a small, relatively unimportant sin or fault.

The gossip column delighted in reporting every minor peccadillo of the city's socialites.

Worked Example

Forgetting to return a library book on time hardly counts as more than a peccadillo.

This wasn't a serious offense -- it was a small, forgivable slip barely worth mentioning, which is exactly a peccadillo.

How Strong Is It? — slip → scandal → peccadillo

slip vs. peccadillo

slip vs. peccadillo: A slip is any small, ordinary mistake; a peccadillo carries a slight moral flavor, a tiny lapse rather than a competence error.

scandal vs. peccadillo

scandal vs. peccadillo: A peccadillo is a small, easily forgiven fault; a scandal is a serious, public wrongdoing that damages someone's reputation.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — pecca

root — pecca: to sin (Spanish/Latin (peccare))

suffix — -dillo

suffix — -dillo: diminutive, small (Spanish)

Put it together

Put it together: Peccadillo comes from Spanish pecadillo, a diminutive of pecado ('sin'), itself from Latin peccare ('to sin') -- literally 'a little sin.'

Use the root in a new word: impeccable

Use the root in a new word: impeccable: The same peccare root gives us impeccable -- a word you already met earlier in this course, from im- 'not' + peccare, literally 'unable to sin.'

Word Choice

Peccadillo almost always carries a light, forgiving tone -- it's used for faults that are easy to overlook or even find charming, not genuine wrongdoing.
